lines.text: This week, Indian AI lab Sthanika unveiled Sieve version three,
and it just tied for first globally on decision benchmarks,
beating established giants like Perplexity and Jev.
For years, the industry assumed top frontier intelligence
demanded billions of dollars from Silicon Valley monopolies.
Then Sthanika's engineering team tested a new paradigm.
Instead of blindly throwing brute-force parameters at the model,
they streamlined the internal reasoning pathways.
The result? It scored number one globally
on complex decision benchmarks that crush larger systems.
